papers.title: Parameter Optimization on the Fabrication of Al-10Si-0.4Mg Alloy Using Selective Laser Melting Process
papers.abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) technology has advantages in building free shape and simplification of manufacturing process. In order to manufacture the high quality parts, it is important to find out the optimum fabrication parameters such as laser power, scan speed, scan pitch and so on. In this research, the fabrication conditions under high power and high scan speed were investigated to fabricate the sound parts of Al-10Si-0.4Mg alloy using a SLM machine equipped with a 1 kW single mode fiber laser. As a result, the effective process window in the process map of the laser power and the scan speed was found out by evaluating the density of the specimens. The range of the energy density that showed high relative density of the parts was 35~80 J/mm3, and it was similar to the result reported by other researches. In the case of the laser power of 700 W, it was found that the relative density keeps high value even at a scan speed of 2200 mm/s. Thus, it was found that the sound parts can be fabricated at high scan speed by increasing the laser power. And the optimum scan pitch was similar to the laser spot size.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究铝合金SLM工艺参数优化，未涉及生物医学植入物、多孔结构或力学性能测试。
llm.why_not_core: No biomedical context, no porous structures, no stress shielding or stiffness matching, no mechanical testing beyond density, no surface roughness or osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 优化高功率高扫描速度下Al-10Si-0.4Mg合金的SLM工艺参数
summary_zh.method: 系统改变激光功率、扫描速度和扫描间距，通过密度评估确定工艺窗口
summary_zh.result: 有效能量密度范围35~80 J/mm³，700W功率下扫描速度可达2200 mm/s
summary_zh.validation: 通过相对密度测量验证工艺参数的有效性

summary_en.motivation: To optimize selective laser melting parameters for fabricating sound Al-10Si-0.4Mg alloy parts under high power and high scan speed.
summary_en.method: Systematically varied laser power, scan speed, and scan pitch, and evaluated specimen density to determine the effective process window.
summary_en.result: The energy density range for high relative density is 35-80 J/mm³, and high power (700 W) allows high scan speed (2200 mm/s) while maintaining density.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed by measuring the relative density of SLM-fabricated specimens.

papers.title: Fracture Toughness Behaviour of 316L Stainless Steel Samples Manufactured Through Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) is a relatively new manufacturing technique which offers many benefits. However the utilisation of SLM manufactured components depends on the assurance of their integrity during operation. Fracture toughness testing (JIC) has been performed on as-built compact tension fracture mechanics samples manufactured in three orthogonal directions. When the crack growth plane was transverse to the interface of the build layers, the fracture toughness values were found to be similar to those manufactured using conventional techniques. However, the fracture toughness is significantly reduced when the crack plane is parallel to the interface of the build layers. Simple heat treatments have been performed on Charpy fracture samples and the resulting impact energy values indicate that the fracture toughness of a component may be improved by heat treatment.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM 316L不锈钢的断裂韧性，未涉及多孔结构或应力遮挡，与生物医学植入物方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses solely on fracture toughness of bulk 316L stainless steel, with no mention of porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue, or biomedical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究SLM 316L不锈钢的断裂韧性各向异性。
summary_zh.method: 对三个方向的紧凑拉伸试样进行JIC测试，并进行热处理后的夏比冲击试验。
summary_zh.result: 裂纹面垂直于层界面时韧性与传统相当，平行时显著降低。
summary_zh.validation: 采用标准断裂力学实验和夏比冲击试验。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the fracture toughness anisotropy of 316L stainless steel manufactured by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: JIC testing was performed on compact tension specimens built in three orthogonal directions, and Charpy impact tests were conducted after simple heat treatments.
summary_en.result: Fracture toughness values were comparable to conventional when the crack plane was transverse to build layers, but significantly reduced when parallel.
summary_en.validation: Standard fracture mechanics testing and Charpy impact testing.

papers.title: Stress and Distortion Simulation of Additive Manufacturing Process by High Performance Computing
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation is an efficient way to better understand the thermal and mechanical evolution during metal additive manufacturing (AM) and to design and optimize the process. However, with today’s computational tools, pass-bypass thermal-mechanical numerical simulation of the metal AM process is extremely time-consuming. In this study, a new finite element code recently developed in house at Oak Ridge National Lab was used for additive manufacturing simulation. Our new code effectively utilizes GPU based high-performance computers to allow for realistic simulation of the transient thermal and mechanical response of materials during additive manufacturing. A benchmark study on a cylinder model by powder bed selective laser melting was carried out and distortion profile was compared to the experimental measurements. The accuracy and efficiency of the code was also demonstrated by analyzing a wire and arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) model which consists of a base plate and four deposited layers.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要关注增材制造过程的热-力学模拟和高性能计算，未涉及生物医学植入物的多孔结构设计或力学性能评估，与用户研究方向的相关性较低。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on GPU-accelerated simulation of thermal distortion in metal additive manufacturing, with no mention of porous structures, stress shielding, stiffness matching, LPBF fabrication of biomedical implants, mechanical testing, or surface characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 金属增材制造过程模拟耗时，需高效计算方法。
summary_zh.method: 开发基于GPU的高性能计算有限元代码，模拟热-力学过程。
summary_zh.result: 成功模拟了激光粉末床熔融和电弧增材制造的变形，与实验吻合。
summary_zh.validation: 通过圆柱模型的变形实验数据进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To accelerate the computationally expensive thermal-mechanical simulation of metal additive manufacturing processes.
summary_en.method: A GPU-based finite element code was developed to simulate transient thermal and mechanical responses during additive manufacturing.
summary_en.result: Accurate distortion profiles were obtained for both powder bed fusion and wire-arc additive manufacturing benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Experimental distortion measurements on a cylinder model validated the simulation accuracy.
